turns.therapist: Hi Yvette, I'm glad you're here. What feels most important for us to talk about today?
turns.client: I don’t know, I guess I just feel like I had plans to enjoy the movie, but then my friend called. It’s not really a big deal, right? I mean, it’s just how things go sometimes. People need support, and I felt like I had to be there for her.

turns.therapist: It sounds like you felt a sense of responsibility to support your friend, even though you had plans for yourself. That can be tough when your own expectations clash with someone else's needs. What do you think it was like for you to shift from your plans to being there for her?
turns.client: It was just a phone call, you know? I mean, I wanted to watch the movie, but my friend sounded upset. I guess I just felt like I couldn’t let her down. It’s not like I’m always doing this; it just happened to be today. It’s not the end of the world, right? I’ll catch another movie later.

turns.therapist: You felt a mix of wanting to enjoy your movie and being there for your friend when she needed support. turns.client: I don’t know, it just feels like that’s what you do for friends, right? I mean, it’s not like I do this all the time. Sometimes you just have to step up when someone needs you. I guess I’ll just make plans to do something for myself later. It’s not like I can always put myself first.

turns.therapist: It sounds like you value being there for your friends and stepping up when they need support, even if it means putting your own plans on hold. What do you think it would look like to carve out time for yourself while still being there for others?
turns.client: I guess it might look like trying to set aside some time for myself, but it just feels complicated. I mean, what if someone really needs me? I don’t want to let people down. It’s easier to just support them when they reach out. It’s not like it’s a huge sacrifice anyway. Plus, I can always do something fun later, right?
